title.narrative: Greater Mekong Subregion: Rehabilitation of the Railway in Cambodia Project

description.narrative: The original project is rehabilitating and restructuring the railway in Cambodia. In addition to this, the supplementary financing will be used to (i) establish a new freight and rolling stock maintenance facility at Samrong, 10 kilometers west of Phnom Penh, with sufficient space to meet future multimodal transport requirements; (ii) upgrade or strengthen parts of the main line to enable early initiation of integrated multimodal services; and (iii) establish additional sidings to terminals to facilitate multimodal connectivity. The combination of the original project and the supplementary financing will be referred to as the modified project. The key activities for implementing the new facility at Samrong include design of the facility; procurement of contracts; preparation, approval, and implementation of the resettlement plan for the area; and implementation of works. Strengthening and upgrading of track does not require additional design or resettlement, activities consist primarily of the installation of heavier rails and new sleepers. Installation of additional sidings to terminals requires additional design and minor resettlement. The outcome would be a selectively upgraded railway in Cambodia exceeding the rehabilitation envisaged in the original project, enabling early takeoff of an integrated, railway-based, multimodal transport system.

title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Freight facilities in Samrong and Phnom Penh constructed Indicator: Access to 2 dry ports and 98-hectare freight and maintenance depot constructed Progress/Status: The Government requested removal of the Samrong Intermodal Terminal. An amendment to the project scope has been approved by the ADB Board on 3 october 2014. As a short-term alternative to the intermodal terminal planned for Samrong, the Concessionaire has constructed a hard stand facility at the CWT Dry Port in Phnom Penh, which is now being used for loading and unloading of train cargo. Data Source: Project reports, railway accounts, and user surveys Reports by the restructuring TA consultants Reports of project supervision consultants Project completion report
Actual value:

Output: Freight facilities in Samrong and Phnom Penh constructed Indicator: 232 affected households in Samrong satisfactorily compensated and assisted Progress/Status: This is now taken out of the Project scope, upon request of the Government. Data Source: Updated resettlement plans Independent resettlement monitor reports disaggregated by gender
Actual value:

Output: Rail links to Sihanoukville port and the port in Phnom Penh rehabilitated and extended Indicator: About 15 km of rail links to Sihanoukville container port and the port in Phnom Penh rehabilitated Progress/Status: The Sihanoukville container terminal and the railway track at the Sihanoukville port are complete. Data Source: Project reports, railway accounts, and user surveys Reports by the restructuring TA consultants Reports of project supervision consultants Project completion report
Actual value:

Output: Railway department staffed and operational Indicator: 25 staff transferred to the railway department and adequately trained Progress/Status: Railway Department's capacity building programs to be able to manage concession is completed. Data Source: Reports by the restructuring TA consultants Reports of project supervision consultants Project completion report
Actual value:

Output: Railway link to Thailand reconstructed Indicator: About 48 km of railway line from Sisophon to the Thai border reconstructed Progress/Status: About 42 km completed.
